findings.title: Backup code path skips password check for external-TOTP flow
findings.body: The password check runs only when `!credentials.totpCode`, but the backup-code branch is selected by `credentials.backupCode`. A client can send a valid backup code together with any non-empty `totpCode`, which skips the password verification. Because the backupCode branch is taken first, the totpCode is never validated. A backup code alone then grants login without the password, making it a single factor.

findings.title: Backup code consumption is not atomic
findings.body: The code reads the backup codes, checks them in memory, and then writes the re-encrypted list back with no transaction or compare-and-set. Concurrent login requests can all validate the same code before any of them writes, so a single-use code can be used several times. A concurrent write can also overwrite another request's update.

findings.title: Unvalidated backupCode type crashes handler
findings.body: `req.body.backupCode.replaceAll` assumes the value is a string. A non-string value, such as a number or an array, throws and returns a 500. The client also always sends `backupCode` (possibly an empty string) alongside `code`, and the request is routed only by truthiness. Nothing validates the format or type of the value.

findings.title: Lost-access option unavailable in external TOTP flow
findings.body: When `totpEmail` is set (Google/SAML users with 2FA), the page shows ExternalTotpFooter, which has no 'Lost access' button. Those users cannot use their backup codes. This is also the only flow where the password check is legitimately skipped.

findings.title: formatBackupCode used before its const declaration
findings.body: `handleSetup` calls `formatBackupCode`, which is declared later with `const`. This works only because the call happens at runtime, after render. The blob object URL is also never revoked when the modal closes, so it leaks for the life of the page.
